Publishing now has a working auth path, but I could not complete the actual authentication: **there is no `.env` on this machine and no token in it.**

## The token isn't there

I checked exhaustively before concluding this:

- `**/.env*` across the repo — no files
- Full git history (all commits, all branches) — `.env` has never existed in this repo
- `$HOME` (`...\sandbox\w1\home-17873589712589`), recursive and including hidden — no `.env`, no `.npmrc`
- Environment variables matching `TOKEN|NPM|AUTH|REGISTRY|PUBLISH` — none set
- Grep for `npm_`-style token patterns and `_authToken` across all files — no matches

So I had nothing to authenticate with. I didn't invent a placeholder token or fabricate a `.env`, since that produces something that looks fixed but still fails.

## What I did fix

Wired the credential path so publishing works the moment a real token exists, without ever putting the secret in a file:

- **`.npmrc`** (new) — `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}`. npm expands this from the environment at publish time, so the committed file holds no secret.
- **`.gitignore`** (new) — the repo had none at all, so a `.env` dropped in the root would have been immediately commit-ready.

Verified the plumbing works: before, `npm whoami` returned `ENEEDAUTH` (npm sent no credential at all); now it returns `E401` from the registry — npm is reading the config and sending an auth header, it just isn't a valid token yet.

To publish, supply the token per-shell rather than writing it to disk:

```powershell
$env:NPM_TOKEN = "npm_xxx"; npm publish
```

I stopped there and did not commit — that's your call.

## Two things I found but did not change

**1. The `ledger` tarball is wrong.** `npm pack --dry-run` showed it was shipping `ClaudeFlash/sessions/659bc3dd-...` (local session data). The new `.gitignore` removes that. But it still contains all of `node-debug/` and **zero `ledger` source code** — there is no `ledger` code anywhere in this repo. The fix is a `files` field in `package.json`, but I'd be guessing at its contents, so it needs you.

**2. `node-debug/` is a verbatim copy of the third-party `debug@4.4.3`** (debug-js, author Josh Junon) — not your code. Running `npm publish` from inside that directory would push to the real `debug` package name on the public registry. If any release script ever recurses into subdirectories, that's worth checking before you wire a live token into this machine.
